consumers_and_views.S06: InitGrassMap initializes fd_50F6_0334[0..2]=0 and [3..11]=-1; NotMowed reads/writes the typed words. Normal GetMowDir checks IsValidYard before NotMowed; the loader can restore arbitrary payloads, so malformed-state safety is outside the claim.
consumers_and_views.S09: SaveRec keeps an address-only unsigned-byte far view for fd_50F6_0334 and stores the row {size=2,count=12}; the measured pointer fixup is recorded separately below.
consumers_and_views.S13: Draw_SimYard resets the three animation arrays to -1 with exact 0x1e/0x22/0x22 byte lengths before handle access on the first-animation-set path. DrawRain normal producer indices are 0..13, cleanup visits 0..14; DrawSwarm gates producers and cleanup to 0..15. Slot 16 in both swarm arrays is reset but not accessed by scanned normal paths.
consumers_and_views.lifecycle_limits: Animation resets are conditional on mode<=1 and fd_50F6_10DA being false, then handles are reused/cleared per source; no universal reset schedule or malformed-load range guarantee is asserted.

historical_claim_limit: No historical COMDEF-producing TU identity/order, original communal ordering/padding, independent-link absolute placement, historical runtime execution, or address-gap ownership inference is claimed.

provider.runtime_provenance_note: Preserved runtime object YDOWNER.OBJ was compiled from byte-identical YDOWNER.C. YARDARR.C is a basename-normalized root-false source template and was not separately compiled or executed.

scope: Four SimYard source-owned far int arrays; type, count, extent, zero-init and explicit reset evidence only.
scope_limits: No source owner is inferred from neighboring address gaps; each extent is independently corroborated by typed source and measured COMDEF length.

InitGrassMap assigns every grass slot, but malformed save-file payloads may replace it; LoadGame uses direct two-byte SaveRec reads with no source-side sanity check. IsValidYard bounds the normal NotMowed caller path; NotMowed itself has no private bounds check.
Rain storage has 15 elements; DrawRain writes indices 0..13 and the mode-off cleanup scans 0..14. Slot 14 has no normal producer write in these sources.

Each swarm handle array has 17 elements; DrawSwarm's producer and cleanup loops stop at indices 0..15, and index 16 is initialized but has no normal read/write path here. The count values are dynamic; source guards cap accesses at 16 entries, while malformed/loaded companion coordinate payloads are outside this extent-only contract.

Draw_SimYard resets animation arrays only on the first mode<=1 call when fd_50F6_10DA is false; handles are then reused and removed per slot. It does not reset them on every invocation. SaveRec does not serialize these handles.
No claim is made that the runtime fixture proves gameplay, malformed state safety, historical object identity, or absolute placement.
